title: Bounded error from one-sided error
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every run of $N$ on every binary input uses space at most $s$ of the input length. For each input $x$, suppose there is a time $T$ by which every branch halts, the probability of outputting the one-bit string $1$ is at least $2/3$ when $x\in L$, and every branch outputs the one-bit string $0$ when $x\notin L$. Then for each input there is such a halting time at which the probability of outputting the correct membership indicator is at least $2/3$, while the space bound remains $s$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$L$ is a language of binary strings
$s$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
Every run on every binary input uses space at most $s$ of its input length
For each input, some time $T$ makes every branch halt
On members, output $1$ has probability at least $2/3$ at time $T$
On nonmembers, every length-$T$ choice word produces output $0$
